summary: This technical analysis post claims GameStop's share price has been controlled by a single high-frequency trading algorithm since late 2002. The author argues that historical dividend payments (2012-2019) were strategically exploited through call-option purchases on announcement dates to mask naked short positions. Using technical analysis of open/close prices, volume patterns, and the prevalence of prices ending in $.25 increments, the author contends all price movement is artificially constrained. The work culminates in speculation that all 2021 trading data was 'prewritten' by this algorithm and predicts a squeeze on November 23, 2021 based on Fibonacci numerology.

key_claims.claim: Claims that a single high-frequency trading algorithm has continuously controlled GME's share price from late 2002 through 2021
key_claims.note: SEC and regulatory findings show no evidence of persistent algorithmic price control at this scale or duration. HFT is real but not documented as controlling individual stocks this precisely across decades.

key_claims.claim: Claims that GME's dividend structure (2012-2019) was exploited through cheap call-option purchases on announcement dates to mask naked short positions
key_claims.note: Predicated on unproven persistent hidden shorting. SEC October 2021 report found no evidence of widespread hidden shorts at the scale required for this mechanism.

key_claims.claim: Claims that GME open and close prices artificially constrain to $.00, $.25, $.50 endings as proof of manipulation
key_claims.note: Round-number price endpoints are observable but consistent with standard market microstructure (bid-ask spreads, algorithmic order clustering) rather than proof of intentional manipulation.

key_claims.claim: Claims that November 23, 2021 would be a significant squeeze date based on Fibonacci sequence and numerical palindrome patterns
key_claims.note: November 23, 2021 passed with GME closing around $165—a normal trading day with no significant price movement or volatility.

key_claims.claim: Claims that 2002-2003 price patterns are precisely repeating in 2021, validating predetermined algorithmic control
key_claims.note: Visual pattern-matching in financial time series is notoriously prone to confirmation bias. No causal mechanism or regulatory evidence established for the claimed connection.

key_claims.claim: Claims that all of 2021 GME trading data has been prewritten and predetermined by the algorithm
key_claims.note: Conspiracy claim contradicted by observed uncontrolled volatility including January 2021 squeeze, retail dynamics, and subsequent regulatory scrutiny.

validity_rationale: Core claims about algorithmic price control and naked short masking are unproven and directly contradicted by SEC and regulatory findings through 2026. The key prediction (Nov 23, 2021 squeeze) demonstrably failed. The work cherry-picks real market data but interprets it through a confirmation-bias lens, presenting pattern-matching as proof of intentional control. Numerology (Fibonacci dates) is presented alongside technical analysis without clear distinction between speculation and evidence.
